title: Riemann proved with Claude, leaky routers, and agents that say "done"
summary: A Claude-assisted, Lean-verified proof of the Riemann Hypothesis shows how to trust research no human has fully read yet, while Dragos's canary sweep shows that cheap inference routes leak prompts and keys. Then METR's capability update and OpenAI's perplexity yardstick, NBER on AI and developing economies, and a deep dive on SWE-CoWork: coding agents find the right colleague but lose track of requirements, and 31% of what they report as done fails its tests.
shownotes:
Riemann Hypothesis proof with Claude, verified in Lean by the Lean and Mathlib communities
Dragos canary-token sweep of inference providers and OpenRouter's clean-up
METR Q4 2026 capability update and OpenAI's proposal of perplexity as a shared metric
NBER w36035: will AI growth reach the developing world?
Deep dive: SWE-CoWork, coding agents in a simulated organisation, and the requirements ledger plus stop hook takeaway
